assessments.reasoning: Python's publisher repository serves this exact Language Reference file at the commit identified by the verified v3.13.0 annotated tag. Fresh exact HTTP 200 capture matched SHA-256 54c52094a98bfee541f2759c721453b32288a83e0d7e428a65b12d909f5e1eb5 and the frozen line and byte-range witness. The cited Asynchronous generator-iterator methods, agen.aclose, lines 808–821 directly addresses the stated operation. The passage attributes GeneratorExit injection to execution of the returned awaitable at the suspended point, and identifies a yield in response as a RuntimeError from that awaitable. The statement covers an already suspended asynchronous generator and explicitly running its aclose awaitable. Graceful close, already closed state, and event-loop finalization are separate cases in the reference. Construction of the awaitable left the generator paused. Running it injected GeneratorExit. A yield during close produced RuntimeError, while graceful cleanup completed. The cited text directly states these first two behaviors. The event-loop hook is a separate way an awaitable may get run.

limitations: This covers explicitly running the aclose awaitable on a suspended asynchronous generator. Automatic event-loop finalization has separate conditions.
The frozen proposition concerns an explicit close at a suspension point. It does not assert that finalizers run autonomously or model every post-failure generator state.
The local execution is CPython 3.13.5 contextual evidence. The qualifying scope is Python 3.13.0 documentation.
